question: For which long-horizon agent failures is memory architecture change actually the right intervention, given that planning and instruction errors dominate end-to-end trajectory failures?
evidence_summary: [2604.11978] attributes most long-horizon failures to planning errors, with memory limitation a minority; [2608.15008] finds memory retrieval quality does not transfer to ALFWorld planning success; [2606.24775] finds a no-memory Long Context baseline wins DB-Bench EM.
why_unexplored: Memory research has its own benchmarks and momentum, while end-to-end failure attribution is expensive and newer.
who_needs_it: Research agenda setters deciding whether to invest in memory architectures, planning/reasoning, or instruction-following.
